title: Routing graceful-degradation keyed off error budget burn (region failover + model fallback)
creator: Aisha Bello
project: Tiered SLO definitions + error budget policy
body:
## Context
We’re formalizing tiered SLOs + error budget enforcement. To prevent cascading failures and reduce customer-visible incident severity, routing should automatically “steer away” from unhealthy capacity based on near-real-time burn signals.

This ticket implements graceful-degradation behaviors keyed off error budget burn (and/or fast-burn alerts) for:
- Hosted API (multi-tenant): region failover, model fallback, and protective throttling coordination.
- Dedicated pools (single-tenant-ish): strict guardrails so we do NOT violate isolation/commitments; prefer “within-pool” mitigations first, and only fail over when explicitly allowed.

## Goals
1) Reduce impact radius when a region/model/route is burning error budget (availability/latency/streaming disconnect SLIs).
2) Convert reliability signals into automatic mitigation actions (routing policies) with clear auditability.
3) Keep behavior predictable and tier-aware (Hosted vs Dedicated).

## Non-goals
- Changing contractual SLA language.
- Major runtime architecture changes.
- Fully automated remediation for Private deployments (document guidance only).

## Definitions (working)
- Burn signal: computed burn-rate for a given SLO scope (tier + route class + region + model family) over multi-window periods; sourced from the error budget computation service (ENG-2421) and burn-rate alerting standard (ENG-2420).
- Degradation actions:
  A) Region failover: route traffic away from region R to region R’ for eligible tenants/requests.
  B) Model fallback: route to a compatible model variant (same interface, similar quality tier) when a specific model is unhealthy.
  C) Protective throttling: intentionally reject/slow some requests to protect overall system stability (owned by quota/throttling integration, but we must coordinate triggers).

## Scope & design
### 1) Policy evaluation inputs
Routing policy engine needs a canonical “budget status” signal for scoped dimensions:
- tier: hosted | dedicated
- service: gateway/routing/runtime (for attribution), but routing decisions will primarily use route-level SLIs
- route class: chat/completions streaming vs non-streaming; embeddings; rerank (if applicable)
- region
- model (or model family / model_id depending on cardinality constraints)
- dedicated_pool_id (Dedicated only)

Inputs are expected from Control Plane budget-check API (see control plane PR: redwood/pull_request_18421) OR via cached feed from budget computation job.

### 2) Degradation rules (proposed)
#### Hosted
- If burn is spiking for (region=R, route_class=streaming_chat) and global capacity exists:
  - Prefer region failover for requests with latency-sensitive profile + idempotent safety (streaming requests are not idempotent mid-stream; failover applies at request start only).
  - Fallback to secondary model variant if primary model is unhealthy (availability or 5xx/timeout class failures) and fallback model is in the “compatible set”.
  - If burn indicates system-wide overload (multiple regions or global burn): coordinate with protective throttling mode instead of shifting load and amplifying failures.

#### Dedicated
- Default: no cross-pool failover.
- Allowed mitigations:
  - Within-pool reroute across nodes/replicas.
  - Temporarily disable non-essential features (e.g., optional tool-calling expansions) only if behind feature flag and approved for Dedicated.
- Cross-region failover only if tenant has explicit flag: dedicated_failover_enabled=true and a configured secondary pool/region.
- Model fallback only if customer has pinned “model family” not a strict model version, and the alternative is explicitly whitelisted for that customer.

### 3) Compatibility & safety
Model fallback must ensure:
- API surface compatibility (function/tool calling support, context length, response format constraints).
- Safety/quality constraints: only within same “quality tier” as defined in catalog; no silent downgrade across major families unless customer opted in.
- Observability: emit labels for fallback_reason and selected_fallback_model to enable auditing and postmortems.

### 4) Control plane + routing integration
- Routing service pulls budget status at a bounded rate (cache with TTL, e.g., 30s) to avoid making budget service a dependency in the hot path.
- Policy engine returns an action set (e.g., prefer_region=us-east-1 → us-west-2; fallback_model=A → B) with a reason code.
- All actions are recorded to an audit log stream for later analysis (owner: Jordan Lee / policy engine).

## Implementation plan
1) Define the policy schema additions (tier-aware) for degradation actions and per-tenant overrides.
2) Implement budget signal client in routing service with caching + circuit breaker.
3) Add region failover decision path:
   - Respect tenant data residency and allowlists.
   - Apply only at request start (no mid-stream migration).
4) Add model fallback decision path:
   - Use model catalog “compatible variants” mapping.
   - Add guardrails for Dedicated pinned models.
5) Add metrics/tracing:
   - routing.degradation.action_count{action,reason,tier,region,model}
   - routing.degradation.request_rate_affected
   - sampling on high-volume endpoints to stay within cardinality budgets (coordinate with ENG-2424).
6) Rollout:
   - Phase 1: dark launch (compute recommended action, log only).
   - Phase 2: Hosted only, low % canary by region.
   - Phase 3: Expand Hosted; enable Dedicated only for explicit opt-in tenants.

## Acceptance criteria
- When a burn signal exceeds configured threshold, routing takes one of the configured actions (failover/fallback/throttle-coordination) within <= 60s.
- No increase in error rate for non-burning scopes (avoid “chasing” failures into healthy regions).
- Dedicated guardrails verified: no cross-customer leakage, no unintended cross-region routing.
- Clear auditability: for any request, we can answer “did we degrade?” + “why?” + “what action?”
- Runbook links updated for oncall (tie-in to error budget exhaustion response runbook).

## Open questions
- Thresholds: do we key off multi-window burn alerts (fast-burn) or the underlying burn-rate numbers? Proposal: use burn-rate numbers with the same multi-window logic as alerting (to minimize divergence).
- Latency burn vs availability burn: for region failover, latency burn should be sufficient (p99/p95). For model fallback, availability/5xx/timeout burn should be primary.
- How do we treat streaming disconnect burn? Depends on classification work (ENG-2428). For now: only use disconnect burn to trigger model fallback (not region failover) until we trust the attribution.

## Links
- Project umbrella: ENG-2417
- Burn-rate alerts: ENG-2420
- Budget computation service: ENG-2421
- Release gating: ENG-2422 (routing should not require gates, but we should align on shared budget status API)
- Tier propagation metrics: redwood/pull_request_18433
- Routing graceful degradation implementation: redwood/pull_request_18455 (in progress)

## Notes on risk
- Risk: region failover can overload the target region and worsen global reliability. Mitigation: require spare-capacity signal + cap traffic shift rate.
- Risk: model fallback changes output quality. Mitigation: only within whitelisted compatible sets; add customer opt-outs; surface in Console/event logs.
- Risk: budget service dependency. Mitigation: cached reads + circuit breaker; default behavior is “no degrade” when signals unavailable (but alert).
comments: 2026-01-23 (Aisha Bello): Created. Goal is to make error budgets a leading indicator with real mitigations, not just dashboards. Routing is the most immediate lever; need tight coordination with policy engine + control plane budget API.
2026-01-28 (Mina Haddad): +1 on cache + circuit breaker. We can’t add a new synchronous dependency in request path. Suggest TTL 30s with jitter and a hard cap on refresh QPS per routing pod.

2026-02-03 (Jordan Lee): Policy schema proposal: add `degradation_rules` keyed by tier + route_class, with per-tenant overrides. Will draft in parallel; please confirm compatibility source-of-truth (catalog vs config).

2026-02-05 (Lauren Bishop): Dedicated constraints: we can’t silently fail over across regions for most customers; some have data residency constraints. If we do anything for Dedicated, it must be explicit opt-in with a pre-provisioned secondary pool and clear comms to Support/CS.

2026-02-07 (Ravi Menon): Model fallback: propose using catalog “compatible_variants” mapping (maintained by Applied ML + runtime team). Need a strict allowlist for Dedicated tenants pinned to a version. Hosted can be looser but still within same quality tier.

2026-02-12 (Elena Popov): Region failover should incorporate capacity signal (scheduler available tokens/sec or queue depth) to avoid shifting load into a saturated region. We can consume existing routing capacity feed; will sync with Keiko/Gabe.

2026-02-16 (Sergio Costa): Observability ask: make sure we emit `fallback_reason` and `selected_backend` labels in a way that doesn’t explode cardinality. Prefer enumerated reason codes and model-family rather than full model_id in high-volume metrics.

2026-02-19 (Ravi Menon): Draft implementation underway in redwood/pull_request_18455. Currently supports Hosted-only model fallback triggered by synthetic “burn risk” flag (temporary). Next step is wiring to real budget status API once ENG-2421 lands.

2026-02-21 (Aisha Bello): Please align triggers with burn-rate alerting standard (multi-window). We don’t want routing to use a different notion of ‘fast burn’ than paging; otherwise oncall will have a hard time reconciling behavior.

2026-02-24 (Ravi Menon): Status: In progress. Added dark-launch logging (action recommendation only) behind `routing_degrade_darklaunch`. Next: implement rate-limited region failover (Hosted) gated by `allow_region_failover` + residency rules. Dedicated behavior remains no-op unless opt-in. Targeting canary in us-east-1 first week of March.
